job.title: Head of Policy and Public Affairs
job.description:
About the Organisation 

NSW Farmers is Australia’s largest state farming organisation, representing farmers and rural communities across New South Wales. For more than 125 years, it has been a trusted voice for the sector, shaping policy and advocating for a strong and sustainable agricultural industry. The organisation works closely with members, government and industry to influence outcomes and support the long-term success of regional communities.

The Role 

As a member of the Executive Team, the role contributes to organisation-wide strategy, performance, financial sustainability and stakeholder leadership, and plays a key role in supporting the CEO to deliver the Association's strategic objectives.  

Serving as the central integrator across policy, communications, and public affairs, the role ensures a consistent narrative, aligns activities with organisational priorities, works cross-functionally to maximise impact, strengthen external influence, support membership growth and retention, develop strategic partnerships and projects, and deliver tangible value to members and the Association. 

Key Responsibilities 

Policy Leadership and Advocacy 
  • Lead NSW Farmers' policy and advocacy agenda, identifying and responding to issues impacting members and the agricultural sector.  
  • Build influential relationships with government, industry and key stakeholders to drive policy outcomes.  
  • Develop and deliver advocacy strategies that strengthen the organisation's impact, reputation and influence.  
Public Affairs and Communication 
  • Lead the organisation's public affairs and communications strategy across media, digital and member channels.  
  • Ensure consistent, compelling messaging that supports advocacy priorities and member engagement.  
  • Enhance the visibility, reputation and influence of NSW Farmers among members, stakeholders and the broader community.  
Organisational Alignment and Member Value 
  • Partner across the organisation to align policy, advocacy and communications initiatives with strategic priorities. 
  • Drive activities that support member acquisition, retention and engagement.  
  • Identify and develop partnerships, projects and opportunities that create value for members and support organisational sustainability.  
Stakeholder Engagement and Governance 
  • Provide strategic advice and reporting to the CEO, Board and Executive Team.  
  • Manage engagement with Executive Council, committees and key member groups.  
  • Ensure strong governance, accountability and alignment across policy, advocacy and public affairs activities.  
Leadership and Living Our Values 
  • Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team focused on delivering measurable outcomes.  
  • Contribute as a member of the Executive Team to organisational strategy, performance and continuous improvement.  
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, wellbeing and excellence across the organisation. 
Candidate Profile 

Experience 
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in public policy, law, economics, political science, government, international relations or a related discipline. 
  • Senior experience in policy, advocacy and public affairs. 
  • Strong government and stakeholder engagement experience. 
  • Sound understanding of legislative, regulatory and parliamentary processes. 
  • Experience leading high-performing teams and working with Boards and governance structures. 
  • Ability to build partnerships that create practical member value. 
Highly Regarded 
  • Knowledge of agriculture, regional communities or farming businesses. 
  • Understanding of key issues affecting NSW farmers. 
  • Networks across government, industry, media or member-based organisations. 
  • Experience supporting membership growth and organisational influence. 
Leadership style 
  • Strategic, collaborative and values led. 
  • A clear communicator who unites policy, communications and public affairs. 
  • Credible with senior stakeholders and confident navigating complex issues. 
  • Commercially aware, politically astute and member focused. 
  • Practical, outcomes-oriented and comfortable driving change. 
  • An empowering leader who builds capability and supports career development. 
Why join us 

With a strong focus on delivering an integrated communications and advocacy strategy, you will lead high-impact initiatives that support membership growth, strengthen external influence, foster strategic partnerships, and deliver tangible value to members while helping secure the long-term sustainability and success of Australian agriculture. 

As a member of the Executive Team, reporting to the CEO, you will play a key role in shaping policy outcomes, strengthening stakeholder relationships, and enhancing the voice of NSW farmers across government, industry and the broader community. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious leader to further develop their executive capability, broaden their influence and progress their career in a highly visible, purpose-led role.

job.title: Head of Impact, Stepping Stone House
job.description:
About Stepping Stone House

Stepping Stone House exists to end child and youth homelessness in Australia.
Supporting children and young people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, the organisation provides safe housing, therapeutic care and long-term pathways to independence.  What sets Stepping Stone House apart is its commitment to supporting young people well beyond crisis, with aftercare programs extending through to age 30 to help create lasting outcomes.
Today, Stepping Stone House supports almost 100 young people and has ambitious plans to more than double its impact over the coming years.  With strong Board backing, significant investment in growth and a clear strategic vision, the organisation is entering an exciting new chapter.  Based in Rockdale with hybrid flexibility, this is an opportunity to join a values-led organisation where people genuinely come first.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the CEO, the Head of Impact will lead all fundraising, philanthropy, partnerships, marketing, communications, volunteering, advocacy and government funding activity across the organisation.

This is far more than a traditional fundraising leadership role.
You'll inherit a team of seven and lead the development of a high-performing Impact function that is expected to grow significantly over the coming years.

The Board has a genuine appetite for investment and growth, with plans to expand the team to approximately 14 people as revenue increases.

The organisation has set ambitious income targets, including significant growth across philanthropy, government funding, partnerships and major giving.  You'll play a central role in shaping and executing the strategy that enables Stepping Stone House to support more young people and create greater long-term impact.

This role will suit an experienced fundraising or impact leader who enjoys building teams, driving performance, creating sustainable growth and leading from the front.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and deliver the organisation's long-term Impact and fundraising strategy
  • Lead fundraising across philanthropy, partnerships, events, trusts and foundations, grants, government funding and individual giving channels
  • Build and scale new revenue streams including major gifts, bequests and regular giving programs
  • Drive brand awareness, marketing and communications initiatives to strengthen community engagement and support
  • Work closely with the CEO, Board and Care team to maximise strategic funding opportunities
  • Strengthen donor journeys, stewardship and supporter engagement programs
  • Lead, coach and develop the Impact team, creating a culture of accountability, performance and collaboration
  • Utilise data and Salesforce insights to drive decision making, forecasting and performance outcomes
  • Represent the organisation externally with key donors, partners, government stakeholders and community leaders
About You

You may come from a fundraising, philanthropy, partnerships, marketing or broader impact leadership background.

Most importantly, you'll be an accomplished leader who has successfully driven growth, built high-performing teams and delivered measurable outcomes.

You will bring:
  • Senior leadership experience across fundraising, philanthropy, partnerships, impact, marketing or communications
  • Demonstrated success growing revenue and developing sustainable funding streams
  • Experience leading and developing teams through periods of growth and change
  • Strong commercial acumen and a data-driven approach to performance
  • Exceptional relationship-building and stakeholder management capability
  • Confidence engaging with Boards, executive leaders, major donors and strategic partners
  • The ability to set high standards, have courageous conversations and inspire high performance
  • A genuine connection to the mission of supporting vulnerable young people
Why Join Stepping Stone House?

This organisation has built a culture that genuinely prioritises its people.
Employees describe a workplace that is respectful, supportive and values-driven, with a strong sense of purpose and psychological safety.  The organisation invests heavily in learning and development, creates meaningful opportunities for staff to connect directly with young people and works hard to ensure employees feel supported both personally and professionally.
Additional benefits include:

  • Incentive program

Perhaps most importantly, you'll join an organisation where the work you do directly contributes to changing the lives of young people who need it most.
